_readme: Calibration set for DLD (Digital Logic Design), measured against
'Fundamentals of Logic Design' (Roth & Kinney) plus the four assignment PDFs
and the Karnaugh map quick reference.
'covered' questions are drawn from what the Roth book actually teaches, in
the words a third-semester student would use -- not in the book's own
phrasing, because a student who could phrase it the book's way would not
'off_topic' leans deliberately NEAR-domain. Analog electronics, computer
architecture and VLSI fabrication all sit one course away from digital logic
and share its vocabulary, so they score far higher than a random subject
would. Those are the questions that decide whether the threshold is honest:
a set of off-topic questions about cookery would let almost any threshold
ALIGNMENT_REFUSAL_THRESHOLD is GLOBAL, not per-course. A value that works
here must also still work for CSW2 and CS-C -- re-run all three after any
ingest and take the value that separates covered from off-topic in every
covered: How do I simplify a Boolean expression using a Karnaugh map?
What is the difference between a full adder and a half adder?
How does a D flip-flop differ from an SR latch?
What are minterms and maxterms, and how do I write a sum-of-products form?
How do I convert a number from binary to hexadecimal?
What is a state table and how do I use it to design a sequential circuit?
How do De Morgan's laws let me rewrite a NAND gate as an OR gate?
What is the difference between a multiplexer and a decoder?
off_topic: How do I bias a common-emitter BJT amplifier for maximum swing?
What is the difference between a Mealy machine and a Turing machine's tape?
How does branch prediction work in a superscalar CPU pipeline?
What causes latch-up in CMOS fabrication and how is it prevented?
How do I write a Django model field and choose its type?
What does the operational amplifier virtual short concept mean?
How is a Fourier transform used to analyse an analog signal's spectrum?
How do I calculate the resonant frequency of an RLC circuit?
